title: Why 1.1.1.1 doesn't pass EDNS client subnet
why: EDNS client subnet leaks requester IP to authoritative DNS; Cloudflare refused to forward it for privacy, breaking geo-based DNS CDNs like archive.is.

title: Anecdote about a huge legacy codebase
why: Vivid first-hand account of flag-laden legacy code and test farms, but it is mostly venting without a transferable lesson.

title: How HN's second-chance pool re-ups stories
why: Moderators pick overlooked stories into a pool; software randomly lobs them onto the front page so the community decides whether they survive.

title: Apology in a conference harassment dispute
why: Personal apology and grievance about a conference incident; no technical or informational takeaway.

title: Why Norvig chose Python for teaching AI
why: Python matched textbook pseudocode best, so students mapped algorithms easily; Lisp still has an edge for large projects and compiled speed.

title: How to check if HN has banned a site
why: Killed stories stay visible to users with showdead on; submit a link and see whether it appears on the new page immediately.

title: Why Uber's rider app has thousands of scenarios
why: Country-specific features and experiments from 40-50 teams make a simple-looking app enormously complex; payments alone spans dozens of screens.

title: Why e-ink devices cost so much
why: E-Ink licenses pigment film to manufacturers who face proprietary drivers and few datasheets; the company's control of the supply chain keeps display costs high.

title: How to present a Show HN post well
why: Use Show HN only for working projects people can try; put the site in the URL field, add a backstory comment, and avoid marketing language.

title: How a YouTube page change broke Edge acceleration
why: A hidden empty div over YouTube videos made Edge's hardware-acceleration fast path bail, erasing its battery-life advantage, per a former Edge engineer.

title: Why Go built its own toolchain and stacks
why: Standard C ABIs lacked segmented or growable stacks and precise GC pointer info, so Go had to build its own toolchain to support them.

title: Why adding generics to Go is hard
why: Generics require type inference that stays understandable and explainable to programmers; C++ inference needs pages of spec, and design mistakes are permanent.

title: Quote venting about Oracle
why: A quoted rant about Oracle's corporate character; opinion and insult with no technical or informational content.

title: The actual Hacker News front-page ranking formula
why: Score is divided by a power of hours since posting plus two, with penalties for no-URL posts, buried items and gagged accounts; a classic reference.

title: Solidity's surprising defaults and integer pitfalls
why: Mutable-by-default state, implicit copy semantics, wrapping integers and literal-dependent division make Solidity contracts easy to get wrong.

title: Scale deep before scaling wide or high
why: Before adding machines or bigger boxes, strip abstraction and use better algorithms on one machine; modern CPUs and SSDs handle far more than assumed.

title: Investor defends a subscription company
why: Defensive investor reply about customer satisfaction and a single complaint; no transferable technical or informational lesson.

title: HN's second-chance pool and how to nominate stories
why: Mods and reviewers feed overlooked submissions into a hopper that software randomly lobs onto the front page; interest decides whether they stay.

title: Practical steps from freelancer to consultant
why: Raise rates repeatedly, build specialty practices, bill by the day, take end-to-end responsibility for outcomes, and drop clients who abuse scope.

title: Developer evangelist responds to PyCon dispute
why: Personal response in a harassment controversy about jokes and a photo; no technical lesson and mostly argument.

title: Why Nagle's algorithm and delayed ACKs clash
why: Delayed ACKs bet on a quick reply and usually lose; combined with Nagle this causes the 200ms stalls, and TCP_QUICKACK helps, per Nagle himself.

title: Using FCRA and FDCPA to dispute debts
why: A debt validation letter starts a 30-day clock during which unverified tradelines must be removed, and the FDCPA requires collectors to pause collection until they verify.

title: Why HN's non-siloed design breeds misunderstanding
why: In communities where everyone shares one space, people meet hostile views unexpectedly, unlike self-segregated internet forums where conflict is expected.

title: Accusation that a language author is a fraud
why: Ad hominem accusation of fraud over a project's claims; it is an argument rather than an explanation of anything technical.

title: How clearinghouse collateral drove the Robinhood crunch
why: Trades settle days later, so clearinghouse collateral requirements rise with volatility, forcing brokers to post cash when a stock spikes.

title: Why Windows 8 design decisions went wrong
why: Designers who rarely use Windows overruled usability-tested engineering concerns, such as removing the Start button and the all-white title bars.

title: Why esbuild's Go parser beat its Rust version
why: Go compiled far faster and ran slightly faster; Rust's stack use across match branches overflowed on nested syntax, and destructors added cost.

title: Why truly global remote hiring is hard
why: Hiring across countries means following each country's employment law on vacation, holidays, termination and taxes, making cost and legal risk very uneven.

title: How automakers caused the chip shortage
why: Carmakers cancelled chip orders in 2020 expecting a slump; suppliers reallocated fab capacity, then demand rebounded and chips could not be restored quickly.

title: How flagging and killing work on HN
why: Flags downweight a story and enough of them kill it; flagging comments needs an extra click to the timestamp page, a deliberate speed bump.

title: Founder's account of a vaccine dispute at YC
why: A personal account in a social-media dispute about vaccine access; no technical or informational takeaway.

title: Personal feud with a blogger
why: A personal feud and accusations against another scholar; argument with no transferable lesson.

title: Concrete Solidity pitfalls: 256-bit bytes and strings
why: Everything is 256-bit wide, so byte[] wastes 32x space; strings lack basic operations, and dead allocations are never reclaimed.

title: Argument that XMPP is a failed protocol
why: Strongly argued opinion against XMPP with some implementation experience, but it is mostly a flame war over protocol design.

title: Advice on leaving a demotivating job
why: Personal career and burnout advice rather than technical knowledge; well-meant but not something a technical reader learns from it.

title: Why archive.is relies on DNS geo-routing
why: DNS returns IPs abroad to slow takedowns; Cloudflare's global DNS caching shares one answer across regions, which breaks that scheme.

title: Why clean-room kernel clones are hard
why: Optimized code and hidden internal headers make matching behavior nearly impossible without similarities, per a Windows kernel engineer.

title: Lessons from a CrowdStrike-crashed Linux fleet
why: A security agent update crashed Debian servers across clouds; the lesson is that vendor pushes ignoring staged rollout can bypass your own testing.

title: HN policy on generated comments

title: Why many business strategies can coexist

title: Long horror story about a disastrous software job

title: What Stripe.js collects and why, per cofounder
why: Stripe.js records interaction signals only to detect bots and fraud, not for advertising; sites skipping it face more fraud.

title: Spacing homework to build durable retention
why: Mixing old and current material into homework and opening class with questions left students retaining the course months later.

title: When to enable TCP_NODELAY and QUICKACK
why: Delayed ACKs bet on quick replies and usually lose; on Linux, enable TCP_QUICKACK unless the application is unusual, and TCP_NODELAY has similar effects.

title: Why Chrome avoids a master password
why: The OS user account is the only real permission boundary; a master password would give users false security, since account compromise exposes everything anyway.

title: Political essay about startup boards
why: Political argument about ideological tests for company boards; opinion with no technical or informational content.

title: How companies can pay open source maintainers
